subject: Console: request to surface cost allocation and per-customer pivots
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Console: request to surface cost allocation and per-customer pivots

Team —

Quick ask from sales/finance: ACME (prospect) asked for a lightweight view in Console that shows cost broken down by customer segment and product route so they can validate unit economics before committing to Dedicated. We don't need a full billing export; they want an operational view to answer: which routes and models drive the most token spend for a given account segment (e.g., trial vs. paid), and whether latency SLOs correlate with high-cost routes.

Desired surface in Console (first-pass):
- Pivot by customer segment (account tag) x route_id: token_count, $cost_estimate (token * current unit rate), median latency, p95 latency
- Drill to sample requests (trace ids) for top cells
- Quick filter for model_variant / quantization flag and region
- Export CSV of the pivot and a linkable Drive report

What I need from infra/product:
- An API (or console query) that can join observability traces with billing metadata (route_id, account_tag, model_variant) for a rolling 30d window
- UI: pivot grid + compact heatmap, with ability to pin a saved view to project dashboards
- A short-term rollout plan: 2-week spike for data plumbing, 3-week UI iteration, beta in Console for selected accounts (ACME + 2 others)

Attached: mockups/cost-pivot-wires.pdf (very rough)

Priority: high (sales is asking before next exec call). Can we kick off a sync? I'm happy to run the scope doc.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: request to surface cost allocation and per-customer pivots

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick ask from sales/finance: ACME (prospect) asked for a lightweight view in Console that shows cost broken down by customer segment and product route...

Thanks Jonas — this is a clear ask. A couple of clarifying Qs before we scope:
1) What is the authoritative "account_tag" mapping? Is that coming from our billing system or from sales CRM?
2) For the cost_estimate, do you want live unit pricing (hosted rates) or normalized cost-per-token from infra? The visualization and alert thresholds change depending on which we use.
3) Any privacy/PII constraints if we surface example requests for paid accounts?

Proposed next step: 30-min working session with Dev + Evelyn + Jonas to align on data join and privacy. I'm available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

—Grace
Product Manager, Console
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Console: request to surface cost allocation and per-customer pivots

Grace / Jonas —

Quick technical notes from infra side:
- We can produce a daily materialized view that aggregates tokens by (account_id, route_id, model_variant, region) for 30/90 day windows. That will give token_count and median/p95 latencies.
- Joining billing (charges) to that view requires a stable account mapping key. If sales supplies account_tag as an attribute on requests (or in onboarding metadata), the join is straightforward. If not, we'll need a mapping table (cost: small DB work).
- Exposing sample request traces: we must be careful. We can return trace ids and request timestamps and a sanitized payload link (no user PII) — requires an opt-in flag for accounts to allow sample extraction.
- Performance: computing pivots on-demand is heavy; suggest pre-aggregated cubes updated daily and a fast cache for UI queries.

I'll add a short spike runbook: data sources, query plan, expected storage/cost impact. ETA for spike: 2 weeks if we carve out infra tickets.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 21:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: request to surface cost allocation and per-customer pivots

Jonas / Grace —

From a finance perspective a couple of constraints: 
- The "$cost_estimate" column must be labeled as an *estimate* and should be based on the unit rates applicable to the account (committed vs. pay-as-you-go). For deals with committed discounts we need mapping to the deal_id so ACME's numbers match procurement expectations.
- For exportable CSVs used in procurement calls, include the deal_id column and an applied-unit-rate column.

I can provide a mapping file for current pilot accounts (attached). For privacy, sample requests must not include customer PII — we should default to anonymized request hash and timestamp.

—Evelyn
VP, Finance
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Console: request to surface cost allocation and per-customer pivots

Thanks — attaching the account-segment map and a CSV with the pilot accounts. I'm fine with the "estimate" label. For the rollout:
- Jonas: I'll run the ACE (acceptance) criteria doc and own stakeholder comms
- Dev: spike and data schema (2 weeks)
- Grace: UI mock -> beta in Console (3 weeks)

Attached: acct-segment-map.csv

Jonas
